title: Unratified changes to the Freezer Multisig signers must be presumed malicious, not merely irregular
content:
A.6.1.1.3.2.6.1.2.1.2.2.3.5 governs the kill switch's own membership at the ecosystem level: "modification of the signers of the Freezer Multisig must be approved through an Atlas Edit Proposal" — Sky Governance, not Keel's Root Edit process.

Two exceptions are permitted, both requiring the departing signer to speak publicly: a self-reported loss of private key access, or an explicit wish to be removed, "in the form of a public Sky Forum post." Both are cases where the signer is *renouncing* power, which is why they can bypass a vote: no one gains authority through them.

The final paragraph is the unusual part. "Any changes to the Multisig signers that do not fall within the two exceptions listed above, or that have not been ratified by Sky Governance, should be questioned immediately and treated as malicious. Where malicious activity is suspected, the Core Facilitator must prepare an expedited Executive Vote so that Sky Governance can vote on removing external security access from the Multisig."

This inverts the usual burden. An unexplained signer change is not an anomaly to investigate before acting — it is malice by default, with a pre-specified response and a named party obliged to initiate it. That matters because the failure mode being defended against is an attacker who has already compromised a key: hesitation while facts are gathered is exactly what the attacker needs, so the Atlas pre-commits to treating ambiguity as attack.

The remedy is also revealing. Sky's response is to remove the multisig's access entirely rather than to correct its membership — sacrificing the emergency capability rather than risking a captured one.
description: Signer changes require an Atlas Edit Proposal, with narrow exceptions for publicly declared key loss or resignation; anything else triggers an expedited Executive Vote to strip the multisig's access.
